raw_response:
I farm 57 mu, so I do not play around too much with risk. If the crop looks hungry and I hold back fertilizer, I lose yield on a lot of land at once, and that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I will mostly do what has worked for people around me and what I have seen with my own eyes. On my maize, I will keep the bigger area because it is steady and easy to sell. I will put enough fertilizer under it and then chase once more, because maize without food just stays thin. I have well water, so I will not let it suffer in the dry spells. For stevia, I will keep a smaller area because it needs tighter watching, more sprays, and more hand work. I will feed it a bit more carefully and water it more times, because if the leaves do not grow well, there is no money in it. I will plough both crops first, because on my land I trust turned soil more than leaving it hard on top. This year I will split the land 42 mu maize and 15 mu stevia, keep inputs on the safe side, and aim for a full harvest instead of saving a little cash and regretting it later.
